Style: a traditional hand-painted watercolour illustration, used as a background for a 2D story adventure game, painted with transparent watercolour and a little opaque gouache on rough cold-press watercolour paper. Technique: loose transparent washes laid with large soft brushes, wet-in-wet blooms and soft bleeding edges in the sky and the water, crisp dried edges where washes overlap, pigment granulation in the darker areas, opaque matte gouache only for a few dark shapes and small light accents, a few dry-brush strokes for stone and wood texture, a faint loose pencil underdrawing that shows through in places, and the texture of the white paper visible everywhere through the paint. Reduction: simplified storybook shapes, few objects, large calm areas of colour, slightly wobbly hand-drawn verticals, no fine clutter, no tiny repeated details, no thin ropes or rigging lines. Palette: limited and muted: deep indigo and blue-violet for the shadows, muted slate-teal for water and glass, grey-green for stone and grass, warm cream for walls, paper white for the highlights, warm ochre and burnt orange only at the light sources and in the band of light at the horizon. It is not a photograph, not a 3D render, not CGI, not a smooth digital painting, no airbrush gradients, no glossy highlights, no lens flare, no bloom, no vignette, not a detailed postcard.

Series rules, identical for every picture of this series. Time of day: late dusk, about twenty minutes after sunset; outdoors and in windows the sky is deep blue-violet with a narrow band of warm orange light at the horizon. Light: the main light comes from the left (outdoors the last warm glow of the sky on the left, indoors a warm lamp or fire on the left side of the room); shadows fall to the right and are cool blue-violet; the right side of the picture is slightly cooler and darker. Lamps, windows and fires are small warm orange pools of light. Camera: straight-on view at standing eye height, no tilt, no fisheye, no wide-angle distortion, vertical lines stay vertical; the eye level (outdoors the horizon line) lies at 40 percent of the picture height from the top. Layout for a game screen: the top tenth of the picture is plain sky, wall or ceiling (it may be cropped); the ground or floor where characters walk is an open, uncluttered strip between about 58 and 72 percent of the picture height from the top; the bottom quarter of the picture is a calm, plain, darker foreground without important objects (a text box will cover it).

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

Do not paint effects that the game animates: the lighthouse lamp, the lantern and the cottage window are only small soft glowing spots without any light beams, rays, glare or halo; no smoke at all from the chimney; no birds in the sky. These effects are animated separately in the game.
